U1: Deploy YARN App into HDFS automatically - orchestrate deployment via manifest
U2: Negotiate with ResourceManager REST-APIs to deploy modules by groups, with appType/appName specifics
U3: Support multiple app instances with deployment properties for different queues/priorities
U4: Make deployer work asynchronously - shell returns quickly, queue deploy operations
U5: Experiment/resolve module dependent JARs to Boot loader for external libraries
U6: Refactor ModuleLauncher contract with Boot's JarLauncher API
U7: Complete documentation and test-cases for JAR resolution
U8: Add support to add external libraries uniformly

Plus cross-cutting: testing, integration, build, etc.

- Use Spring YARN project components

- Use Hadoop YARN REST APIs

- Deployment properties via Spring Cloud Deployer SPI

Assumptions:
- Existing Spring Cloud Data Flow codebase
- YARN cluster available for testing
- HDFS accessible
- Java 17+, Spring Boot 3.x, Spring Framework 6.x
- Team has YARN/Hadoop expertise
- Existing ModuleLauncher to refactor

Now activities with estimates (workdays):

3. Implement YARN ResourceManager REST client (U2) - 5 days

5. Implement multiple app instance support with deployment properties (U3) - 6 days
6. Implement asynchronous deployer with queueing (U4) - 5 days
7. Experiment with Boot loader JAR resolution (U5) - 4 days
8. Refactor ModuleLauncher to JarLauncher API (U6) - 6 days
9. Implement external library support (U8) - 5 days
10. Write documentation for JAR resolution (U7) - 3 days
11. Write test cases for JAR resolution (U7) - 4 days
12. Integration testing across all features - 5 days
13. Unit tests for new components - 4 days
14. Code review and refactoring - 3 days
15. Build and CI/CD updates - 2 days

technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring YARN project components for YARN integration
Leverage Spring Boot's JarLauncher for module launching
Use Hadoop YARN REST APIs (ResourceManager) for application submission and monitoring
Implement asynchronous deployment using Spring's @Async with a thread pool executor
Follow Spring Cloud Deployer SPI for deployment property handling
Use Spring Boot's classloader manipulation for external JAR resolution
Maintain backward compatibility with existing ModuleLauncher interface during refactoring
Store deployment manifests in HDFS using Hadoop FileSystem API
Use Spring Cloud Data Flow's existing deployment property parsing mechanism
assumptions: Existing Spring Cloud Data Flow codebase with ModuleLauncher implementation
Development team has expertise in Spring Framework, Spring Boot, YARN, and Hadoop ecosystem
YARN cluster with ResourceManager REST API enabled is available for integration testing
HDFS is accessible and configured for artifact storage
Java 17+, Spring Boot 3.x, Spring Framework 6.x as baseline
Existing CI/CD pipeline can be extended for new integration tests
AppType=CLOUDDATA and appName=spring-cloud-data-yarn-app are predefined constants
Deployment properties follow existing Spring Cloud Deployer convention (module.*.yarn.*)
External libraries are provided as Maven coordinates or file paths
No major changes to Spring Cloud Data Flow shell/UI required

activities.activity_name: Design and Architecture for YARN Deployment Automation
activities.activity_description: Create technical design for HDFS artifact deployment, manifest structure, and orchestration flow. Define interfaces for deployer, artifact resolver, and YARN client.
Develop functionality to upload YARN application artifacts (jars, configs, scripts) to HDFS using Hadoop FileSystem API. Implement manifest generation and storage.
Build REST client for YARN ResourceManager APIs to submit applications, query status, and manage application lifecycle. Handle authentication, retries, and error mapping.
Develop logic to deploy modules by groups using ResourceManager REST APIs. Handle appType=CLOUDDATA and appName=spring-cloud-data-yarn-app specifics. Implement group-based submission and monitoring.

Add support for multiple YARN app instances via deployment properties (module.*.yarn.app.name). Implement queue/priority configuration per instance. Integrate with Spring Cloud Deployer property parsing.

Refactor deployer to work asynchronously. Implement command queue for deploy operations, thread pool executor, and callback/notification mechanism. Ensure shell returns quickly while operations continue in background.

activities.activity_name: Experiment with Boot Loader JAR Resolution
activities.activity_description: Research and prototype approaches for resolving module-dependent JARs and adding them to Spring Boot's JarLauncher classloader. Test with various dependency scenarios.
Refactor existing ModuleLauncher contract to align with Spring Boot's JarLauncher API. Eliminate duplicate functionality. Ensure backward compatibility during transition.
Develop uniform mechanism to add external libraries (Maven coordinates, local files) to module classloaders. Integrate with deployment properties and Boot loader resolution.
Create comprehensive documentation on resolving and adding JARs to Boot loader. Include architecture, configuration, examples, and troubleshooting guide.

activities.activity_name: Write Test Cases for JAR Resolution
activities.activity_description: Develop unit and integration tests for JAR resolution and classloader manipulation. Cover external library scenarios, dependency conflicts, and edge cases.
Perform end-to-end integration testing of HDFS deployment, YARN submission, multiple instances, async deployer, and external libraries on a real YARN cluster.
Write unit tests for all new components: HDFS client, YARN REST client, async deployer, property parsers, classloader utilities. Target 80%+ coverage.
Conduct peer code reviews, address feedback, refactor for consistency with codebase standards, and optimize performance.
Update build scripts, add integration test profiles, configure CI/CD pipeline for new YARN-dependent tests, and publish artifacts.
